trickyParts: The host's one-shot timer cannot be cancelled (SessionContext.setTimeout returns void and there is no clearTimeout), so a single monotonic generation counter, bumped by every message_start, settle, phase-closed, delivered reminder and session change, is the whole defence against two armed timers sending two reminders. A reviewer should read phase-reminder.ts's armReminder with that in mind.

The continuation is bounded to one per run. The count resets on a tool call, and the reminder's own turn is one in which the worker is being told to call a tool, so gating the continuation on the count alone let a run continue itself without end, with no delay and no turn end for the daemon to see. The simplify pass found this; a separate run-scoped flag fixes it.

A reminder must not reset its own count. On Oh My Pi that is why it is pi.sendMessage with the legion-phase-reminder custom type and not sendUserMessage, which inboundKind would read as the daemon's assignment. On Claude Code the server keeps the exact text it last wrote to the inbox and compares the UserPromptSubmit prompt against it.
Claude Code ignores whatever a StopFailure hook returns, so that event can only record and arm a timer; it is also the one event of the five the pod measurements do not cover.

The npm wrapper package's bin/claude.exe is a stub its postinstall replaces. With --ignore-scripts the stub stays a stub, so the image links node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64/claude. Measured and recorded as a comment on the pull request.

Review round 1 requested changes: four Important and five Minor, all fixed in this round. The four Important were two in the shared machine and two in the daemon, and all four are the failure this issue exists to end. (1) tellArchitect awaits a publish with no deadline, so a turn could reset the count and begin a new run while it was in flight, and the acceptance then marked THAT run reported and silenced its notice; the acknowledgement now applies only to the run whose idempotency key it was minted for. (2) On Claude Code a reminder reaches the worker through the bridge's inbox, which can refuse it; deliver had already counted it and spent its one-shot timer, and no turn starts on a line that never arrived, so nothing armed the next reminder and the worker sat idle for good. sendReminder may now answer with a promise, and a rejected delivery is uncounted and re-armed. (3) and (4) are one problem with two faces: an issue's roles share one pod and one volume, and this change let that pod hold both a Claude transcript on the volume and an Oh My Pi session in the database. The pod's volume expectation followed whichever role made the pod, and the lost-volume broadcast dropped every sibling's session. Both now ask the same question of the recorded path rather than of the role (SessionOnIssueVolume, and supervise's new SessionOnVolume). Each of the four has a test that fails without its fix, which I proved by making each fix inert, re-running and restoring it, rather than by inspection. The five Minor: the retry of a publish failure that is not the listener's "no holder" is KEPT and said so at the code (see the next entry); text-call joins quiet in both hosts' legacy-state tests; a Claude role under a session database is given the DSN file pointer so the shim stops exporting the database URL into its environment; claudelaunch.Transcript recognises a transcript for both runtimes where the pod renderer used to; and stall-limits.ts's header no longer says the daemon sets none of the four numbers. The reviewer's fast-follow, the thin forwarders in runtime/tmux/claude.go, is done too.

A departure the reviewer asked to be recorded rather than removed: for a publish failure that is NOT the listener's 404 unclaimed/holder_lapsed, the approved spec says the failure is "logged and dropped", and this implementation instead leaves `reported` false so the run's next delivered reminder publishes again under the SAME idempotency key. It is kept on purpose — one key makes the retry safe, and a listener returning 5xx is exactly when the architect most needs telling — and the code says so at the warn path. Its test is "a notice the listener failed is published again by the run's next reminder, under the same key".
